<result>The new head (`1ade982a1`) closes F1, F2 and F3 as I reported them. I found one new medium issue (a race that can orphan a node at grant time) and two low issues.

**(a) F1 is closed. CONFIRMED.**
- `git diff main...HEAD` shows no change in `rotation/`, `facade/` (`claim_conversion.rs`, `link_sweep.rs`) or `net/cut.rs`. No held set can reach a revoke, downgrade or link-conversion wave. The wave again visits every child ref in the published bodies.
- The new `held_outside` keeps a node only when its winning chain reaches the vault root without the granted folder. The unit test `only_a_winning_chain_to_the_vault_root_holds_a_node_outside` covers the cycle and the self ref.
- At grant time, only a write grantee of an enclosing scope can change the rank. That grantee can already write every node it can make held, so it gets no more access.

**(b) F3, as the PR caused it, is closed. The remaining risk is old (also on main). PLAUSIBLE, no probe: disk is tight and the mechanism is in the code.**
- The grant no longer gives the grantee the id or the vault `ipnsName` of X.
- A write grantee who knows a node id from other sources can still add a ref to it in a body of G:
  - At a higher counter, the owner's rank puts X under G. The owner then reads X with the keys of G, gets a TrustViolation, or sees content the grantee wrote.
  - At any counter, a later revoke or downgrade wave visits the ref, cannot resolve it, and aborts. The `WriteWaveNet::resolve_node` path aborts on any child that does not resolve, so a random id with a random name blocks the revoke the same way.
- This is outside the scope of #2113. I recommend a separate issue: "A write grantee can block their own revoke with a ref that does not resolve."

**(c) The repair rule. CONFIRMED.**
- `blueprint/engine.md`, sync-core rebase table, row "Dual-link (crash residue)": "Observed repair … the child ref's monotonic link counter picks the deterministic loser". `CONTEXT.md` defines "Observed repair" the same way.
- A held node always has its winner outside the granted folder, so each ref that `drop_held_refs` removes is a loser.
- A tie is safe. `held_outside` and `observed_repair` both use `winning_link`, which breaks a tie by the lowest parent id.

**N1. Medium. PLAUSIBLE: a stale render can make the grant orphan a node.**
- Location: `grants/create.rs` (`drop_held_refs` in `reseal_granted_interior`) and `net/rotation.rs` (`promote_scope_root`).
- Mechanism: the held set comes from the owner's rendered snapshot, but the drop removes refs by id from the bodies that are published now.
- Scenario:
  1. Device D1 has a dual-link residue: A (inside G) at counter 1, B (outside) at counter 2.
  2. Device D2 moves X into A at counter 3, then removes X from B.
  3. D1 has not refreshed and grants G. Its held set is {X}, so it removes X from the published A.
  4. No body names X now. X is lost, with no bin entry.
- Fix: pass the winning parent and counter with each held id. Drop a ref only when the published ref still loses to that winner. If not, refuse with `InteriorNotConverged`. Add a test for this.

**N2. Low. PLAUSIBLE. An old hazard class that this PR now also triggers.**
- Location: `sync/drain.rs`, `take_captures`.
- Scenario: a second owner device loaded A but never B. After a read grant, it sees A drop X. Its base no longer holds X, and the name check passes because a read grant keeps the write seed. The device then puts X in the bin and re-keys it, but X is still live under B.
- An ordinary move to an unloaded folder already does the same on main. Record it with the issue above. Do not block this PR on it.

**(d) Fail-closed and encode/decode symmetry. Clean.**
- A body with a ref dropped keeps unique children, so `assert_children_unique` passes.
- The CAS basis and the epoch check run after the drop and do not change.
- `subtree_child_scopes` uses the same rank, so no held node is in the index.
- Every reader, a cold device included, sees no ref to X under G and reads X under B.

The worktree is still unchanged. I put nothing in `~/.claude/scratch/w21/LF-2113/review2/` because I did not build anything.</result>

<result>I opened draft PR #2160 for all three reload bugs, and CI is green on the head commit.

- **PR:** #2160 (DRAFT), https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/2160
- **Branch:** `fix/reload-session-and-folder-view`. It has two commits on `8e5a5b098`.
- **Head SHA:** `59636dae268b350862ed5493127074ecc07e9dd6`

The commits and the PR body have no tool attribution. I ran no review skill and requested no CodeRabbit review.

## Root causes

**#2146 (the account menu shows `[an0n]`):**
- `Web3AuthSession.login` in `apps/web/src/auth/coreKit.ts` kept the email in the memory field `signedInEmail` only.
- The identity token has no email, and the API keeps only a hash of the identifier. Thus `restore()` had no email to read, `email()` returned `null`, and `UserMenu` showed `[an0n]`.

**#2147 (a reload of a nested folder shows `unknown node`):**
- `cold_start` in `crates/engine/src/sync/boot.rs` puts only the root and its direct children into the base snapshot.
- `refresh_focus_on_access` and the tick function `focus_set` get the ancestor chain from that base. No leg lists a folder below the root's children, so `Engine::snapshot` returns `UnknownNode`.

**#2152 (`LOADING VAULT` when the user goes back to the root):** this has the same area as #2147, the cached view after a reload. There are three parts:
1. `createSnapshotStore.assertFocus` in `apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.ts` pulled the snapshot only after `setFocus` resolved.
2. `EngineHandle::command` in `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` held the engine write lock during `SetFocus` and its network legs. It also held the lock during `ManualRefresh`, until the full forced pass ended.
3. `reportFocus` makes the leader relay send a `manualRefresh` on each focus change. The RwLock prefers writers, so the root snapshot waited behind a nocache pass, and that pass is slow after a reload.

## Fixes

**#2146:**
- The session seals `{subject, email}` in the Core Kit `SealedStore` under the key `cipherbox_account_email`. It stores the email only, never a token.
- `restore()` reads the email back only when the subject is the same.
- A wallet login, a logout and a store clear remove the email.
- The email must be stored because the restored auth state cannot give it. The PR body gives this reason.
- I added the key to the storage allow-list in `smoke.spec.ts`.

**#2147:**
- The new function `Engine::locate_folder` lists the vault one level at a time until the base holds the routed folder.
- Each scope uses its own leg. I put the scope grouping into one function, `navigation_legs`, which the file leg also uses now.
- The new constant `MAX_LOCATE_FOLDERS` (256) limits the resolves for one route.
- If the boundary walk has not landed, the function sends a forced pass and waits for it.

**#2152:**
- **Engine:** `Engine::set_focus(&amp;self)` is a new public method. The `Command::SetFocus` arm calls it.
- **Host:** the host runs `SetFocus` under the read lock. It sends `ManualRefresh` under the read lock and waits for `landed()` with no lock. If no tick loop runs, it uses the write-locked command, which is the mint path.
- **Web store:**
  - The store pulls at once on a focus change. This pull stops a pull of the previous folder that is still in flight.
  - The store pulls again when `setFocus` resolves.
  - While that `setFocus` runs, the store ignores `unknownNode`.
- **Staging scenario:** the post-reload `toRoot` wait has the budget `POST_RELOAD_NAVIGATION_MS` = 60 000 ms, with a one-line reason. No other wait changed.

<result>I found no blocking defect. The most important finding is that `locate_folder` holds the engine read lock while it waits for a full forced pass. That wait also explains the 30.3 s first route. I did not build or run the code, and I wrote no notes file.

**1. MEDIUM, CONFIRMED.** File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae073bd472a7182fa/crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, function `locate_folder`. The host `SetFocus` arm in `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` (`EngineHandle::command`) holds the read lock around it.
- **Mechanism.** If `boundary_walk_landed` is false, `locate_folder` files a forced nocache pass and awaits `pass.landed()`. The read lock stays held for the whole wait.
- **Scenario.** A user reloads at `/files/&lt;nested&gt;`. The forced pass meets cold resolves, and the read lock stays held until `overdue()` answers at `refresh_deadline` (30 s). A `logout`, an upload or a create in that time waits for the write lock. `async_lock` prefers writers, so each snapshot read after that writer also waits, and `LOADING VAULT` comes back. This is the #2152 problem with a different cause.
- **No permanent hang.** `overdue()` answers within 30 s. A tick loop that stops drops the sender, and `landed()` returns `Err`.
- **Fix.** Wait only for the boundary walk: add a one-shot signal at the place in `sync/pass.rs` that sets `boundary_walk_landed`, and give the wait a bound. Another option is no wait: return, and use the `SnapshotUpdated` after the walk to run the locate again.

**2. LOW-MEDIUM. Re-file CONFIRMED, effect PLAUSIBLE.** Function: `locate_folder`.
- `boundary_walk_landed` becomes true only when the walk succeeds (`sync/pass.rs`).
- If a hostile shared-scope writer makes each walk reject, each route to a folder that is not in the base files a new full nocache pass. Each of these routes holds the read lock for up to 30 s.
- **Fix.** Use the fix in item 1. Also file no forced pass while `boundary_walk_rejected` is set.

**3. LOW, CONFIRMED.** Function: `refresh_focus_on_access`.
- It reads `now` before `locate_folder`, which can wait for 30 s. The stamps and `focus_folders_due` then use a clock that is up to 30 s old.
- **Effect.** The next visit resolves again too early.
- **Fix.** Read the clock after the locate.

**4. LOW, CONFIRMED.** Function: `locate_folder`, for a routed id that does not exist (for example a deleted folder that the user saved as a bookmark).
- The bound of 256 holds across scopes, because `take(room)` runs before the scope split. It does not hold across routes.
- The stamps prevent a second network read inside the on-access threshold. After the threshold, each route lists up to 256 folders again.
- **Fix.** Accept this, or keep a "not found" result for each target until a pass changes the base.

**5. LOW, PLAUSIBLE.** File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae073bd472a7182fa/apps/web/src/auth/coreKit.ts`, function `clearStore`.
- `removeItem` now runs before `purge`. If `removeItem` throws, `purge` does not run, and the Core Kit secret stays in the store.
- **Fix.** Run `purge` in a `finally`, or remove both slots inside `purge`.

**6. LOW (spec).** File: `tests/web-e2e/staging/workspace.spec.ts`, the post-reload `toRoot` step.
- After the fix, the cached root should paint at once. A 60 s budget lets the staging test pass even if the #2152 fix stops working.
- **Fix.** Keep the default budget for this step, because the root view is held in the cache.

**Question 3: the 30.3 s first route.** The most likely cause is item 1, and it is a defect.
- `refresh_deadline` in `SyncTimingProfile::PRODUCTION` is 30 s.
- The forced pass that `locate_folder` files runs past this deadline on cold resolves. At the 30 s boundary, `overdue()` answers the queued and running requests as `Overdue`. If the route arrives while a poll pass runs, that pass's own boundary answers the request at its 30 s mark.
- `locate_folder` ignores the error. The walk landed early in the pass, so the listing then takes about 0.3 s.
- On the second route the walk has already landed, so the route takes 0.1 s.
- The route needs only the walk, but it waits for the verdict of the whole pass, which the deadline cuts at 30 s.

**Clean gates and checks:**
- **Email at rest.** The email is never stored in clear. AES-GCM binds the storage key name as AAD (`context(key)`). `keptEmail` returns the email only when the subject matches. Wallet login, `logout` and `clearStore` remove the slot, and `purge` also deletes the wrapping key. The unit test checks for no plaintext in storage.
- **ADR: no.** The change adds no key. It adds one display slot under the wrapping key that AGENTS.md rule 4 already names. It has no wire format, no KDF edge and no trust boundary, and a removal costs only one label after a reload. It fails hurdle 1.
- **Host concurrency.** Two `set_focus` calls can now overlap. `locate_folder` and `navigation_legs` release each `RefCell` borrow before each await, and the tick loop already runs these legs beside snapshot reads. The only effects are duplicate resolves and file rows queued for the folder that the user left. No write-locked command can run beside them.
- **`ManualRefresh`.** It holds no lock across `landed()`, and a teardown drops the sender, so the wait cannot outlive it. The `Ok(None)` path that falls back to the write lock checks the state again.
- **Adoption gate.** The new folder legs use the same `FolderRefresh::run`, with per-scope material from `ScopeLegContext::material`. No read path skips the gate.
- **Standards.** The PR follows the comment rules, uses no tracker references, and the `#33 D2` citation is allowed.</result>

<result>I found no significant efficiency problems. The PR makes the seam cheaper overall. Before, each view getter was a separate WASM call that cloned the Rust field, and getters like `children()`, `contacts()`, `grants()` and `state()` each created a new boxed wrapper that nothing freed (a WASM-heap leak on every read). Now a view is serialized once in `encode_view` into a plain JS object, and the TS readers only check its enum values. The `Ts&lt;SiweIntent&gt;` decode was also moved out of the future, so a bad intent rejects without starting the async work.

There are two minor findings, both small:

1. **`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a538311e6524f9594/packages/client/src/worker/commandCodec.ts:313`**
   - **Summary:** `readSnapshot` returns `{ ...view, queueHold: readQueueHold(view.queueHold) }`, but `readQueueHold` hands back the same `hold` it was given, and `SnapshotDescriptor` is now just `SnapshotView`. So the spread copies the object for nothing.
   - **Cost:** one 11-field object copy on every snapshot read. Snapshots are read on every focus poll and every navigation. It is also the only reader that copies; `readSharing`, `readBin`, `readVaultStorage` and the others return their input.
   - **Fix:** call `readQueueHold(view.queueHold);` as a check (or make it return `void`), then `return view;`. The throw on an unknown reason or check name stays, so it still fails closed.

2. **`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a538311e6524f9594/crates/wasm/src/boundary.rs:98-100` and `crates/wasm/src/host.rs:480`**
   - **Summary:** `decode_siwe_intent(&amp;intent.js_value())` clones the JS handle twice. `Ts::js_value()` clones it once, and `from_value(intent.clone())` clones it again.
   - **Cost:** one extra JS heap-slot insert and drop per `siweChallenge`. That is a cold path, so the cost is trivial; the real gain is a smaller API.
   - **Fix:** use `intent.to_rust().map_err(|_| JsError::new("unknown siwe intent"))` in `host.rs` and delete `decode_siwe_intent`. Or make it take `JsValue` by value and pass `intent.js_value()` straight in. An unknown intent is still refused.

Outside my angle, but a real defect in lines this PR changes: in `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a538311e6524f9594/crates/engine/src/record_plane.rs:150-156`, the new `hold_check` was inserted between `is_verdict`'s doc comment plus `#[must_use]` and `is_verdict` itself. As a result:
- `hold_check` picks up `is_verdict`'s doc text and its `#[must_use]`.
- `is_verdict` loses both.

The fix is to move `hold_check`, with its own doc comment, above that doc block.</result>

<result>I found two altitude findings and one optional cleanup. Two other issues are already being fixed by another agent in the working tree.

**1. Which refusals become holds is now decided twice, and a mismatch fails the whole snapshot read** (medium)
- Files:
  - `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a538311e6524f9594/crates/engine/src/wire.rs:466` and `:490` (`QueueHold::of`, `queue_hold`)

  - `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a538311e6524f9594/crates/engine/src/settings.rs:511` (`SettingsRefusal::hold_check`)
- Problem: the drain decides what to hold in `halt_for_bin_load` (`drain.rs:214`, a `_` wildcard holds every non-verdict reason except stranded mint) and in `settings_refusal` / `PlacementRefusal::holds` / `ProviderError::is_deterministic` (`drain.rs:7353`). The PR adds a second list of the same decision in the two `hold_check` methods, and the encoder catches any gap at runtime with `ser::Error::custom("unnamed hold check")`.
- Cost:
  - Suppose someone adds a new non-verdict `DefaultsReason`. The drain will hold on it, `hold_check` returns `None`, and every `snapshot()` read fails while the hold stands. That is the unexplained stall the hold exists to remove, now on the whole folder view.
  - The check names now exist twice: as the `check()` strings and as the kebab-case serde names. Only the `views.rs` equality test keeps them in step.
- Fix: compute the typed check once, where the hold is made, and store it in the hold.
  - Bin index: `halt_for_bin_load` returns `Halt::HeldByBinIndex(BinIndexHoldCheck)` via `reason.hold_check()`, and `QueueHoldReason::BinIndex` carries `BinIndexHoldCheck`. The drain never reads the inner reason (`BinIndex(_) =&gt; return true`).
  - Settings: the release check compares the `SettingsRefusal`, so keep it, but set the check at the same point, e.g. `QueueHoldReason::Settings { refusal, check }` built in `settings_refusal`. Or narrow `SettingsRefusal::Byo` to the seven deterministic `ProviderError` variants so `hold_check` covers every case.
  - Then `QueueHold::of` cannot fail, the "unnamed hold check" error goes away, and fail-closed holds by construction. The worker-side `SETTINGS_HOLD_CHECKS` / `BIN_INDEX_HOLD_CHECKS` refusals stay as they are.

**2. The flaky op-id test is fixed with a random value instead of a fixed one** (low)
- File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a538311e6524f9594/packages/client/test/browser/journalEngine.worker.ts:57`
- Problem: `nextOpId = 10n ** 17n + BigInt(crypto.getRandomValues(...)[0]!) * 1000n`. The 18-digit length is what fixes the flake: no UUID group (12 characters at most) can contain it. The random part adds nothing.
- Cost: the op id changes on every run, so a failure cannot be reproduced exactly.
- Fix: use a fixed 18-digit value, e.g. `private nextOpId = 10n ** 17n;`. The `/^\d{18}$/` assertion in `leadership.spec.ts:378` still holds, and the comment loses "a random … each run".

**3. Optional: the `*Descriptor` names are now plain aliases** (low, could be a follow-up)
- File: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a538311e6524f9594/packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts`, around lines 100–210
- Problem: there are 33 `export type XDescriptor = X` lines. With the hand-written copies gone, each just renames a generated type.
- Cost: every view has two names to look up, and new views will keep adding alias lines.
- Fix: export the generated names directly and move `apps/web` imports onto them. This renames types only, so no field name or kind changes. It is a large mechanical diff, so it is reasonable to leave it out of this PR.

**Already fixed in the working tree, so not counted:** the PR inserted `DefaultsReason::hold_check` between `is_verdict`'s doc comment / `#[must_use]` and its `fn`, and `readSnapshot` spread the whole view just to reassign `queueHold`. Both already have uncommitted fixes in `record_plane.rs` and `commandCodec.ts`.

**Checked and fine at their current depth:**
- `encode_view` is one generic encoder for every view, replacing the per-view `from_facade` code.
- The `Record&lt;Union, true&gt;` allowlists are typed against the generated unions, so they are checked for completeness at build time. They have to live on the JS side to catch version skew.

**Finding 1: `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs`, `RootPublish::run` (lines 2294 and 2370 in the worktree)**
- **Summary:** two `IpnsName` clones that a borrow and a partial move would avoid.
  - Line 2294: `let name = &amp;current.observed.name().clone();` copies the name only to borrow it. `name` is last used at `report_carried_cut` (line 2330), before `current` is moved, so a plain borrow is enough.

- **Cost:** two heap String copies of the name on every scope-root publish. That is trivial next to the network PUT, but it is also extra code.
- **Change:**
  ```rust
  let name = current.observed.name();
  ...
  PublishOutcome::Published { sequence } =&gt; Ok(RepublishBase {
      observed: current.observed.clearing(sequence),
      ..current
  }),
  ```
  Behaviour, floor reads, the lease and error mapping all stay the same.
- **Confidence:** high that it compiles and is correct. The value is low.

**Checked, nothing to change:**
- **`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`, `publish_node`, `let name = &amp;observed.name().clone();`:** this clone is needed. `observed` is consumed by `clearing(..)` in the `acked` match, and `name` is still used after that (`hold_acknowledged`, `adopt_node_record`, `routing_key`). Removing it would mean changing `clearing` to take `&amp;mut self`, which isn't worth it for one small allocation.
- **`Observed::unread`/`record`/`gated` clone the name** where callers used to pass a borrow. This affects the liveness renewal loop, `renewal_walk`, `vault_pointer` (`&amp;Observed::record(&amp;self.name(), ..)` copies an already-owned temporary), and `root_observed` before `park`. Each is one short String per publish. Avoiding them would need a new by-value constructor on the public `Observed` API, which isn't justified.
- **Floor reads run in sequence in `SignatureGate::read` and `PublishBar::read_floors`:** they could be joined, but the tests `cut_on_write_read(2, ..)` and `RaisingFloors` rely on the order "sequence floor, then read, write, cut". Joining them would change that order, so I don't recommend it.
- **Floors read twice in `RootPublish::run` and the write wave's `publish_moved`** (`refuse_below`, then the gate re-reads at the signature): deliberate, and documented as such.
- **`preflight` decodes the whole grant section to get `cut_epoch`:** this does O(grant blobs) work plus a scrubbed copy per root preflight. A commitment-only decode would be cheaper, but it would stop rejecting malformed or duplicate-tag sections there, which changes behaviour. Leave it.
- **`keep_then_commit` callers build the commit future before the snapshot write:** the callees (`advance_sequence_on_unseal`, `PendingAdoption::commit`) are `async fn`, so the future is lazy and no work runs early.
- **`Display for PublishError` and `error.to_string()` in `emit_renewal_failures`:** the same allocation per error as the old per-arm `to_owned()`/`format!`.</result>

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I found one real efficiency problem. Everything else the diff adds is cheap or necessary.

**1. `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:41-62`, `held_outside`: quadratic scan over the whole vault on every new share**

- **Cost:**
  - The `inside` closure runs `is_descendant_of` on every link in the snapshot. `links().iter().filter(|link| inside(link.parent) &amp;&amp; ...)` evaluates `inside(link.parent)` for all L links. For a link outside the granted folder, that walk climbs all the way to the root.
  - Each step of the walk calls `parent_of`, which goes through `winning_link`, then `links_ranked`, then `links_to`. That is an O(L) scan plus a `Vec` allocation and a sort.
  - Total cost is about O(L² · depth) comparisons and O(L · depth) allocations, paid on every share-mint (the non-append path).
  - Example: a 10k-entry vault at depth 6 needs roughly 6×10⁸ link comparisons and about 60k small allocations. In WASM that is noticeable latency.
  - `subtree_child_scopes` next to it only walks the small child-scope index, so it isn't a comparable cost.
- **Cheaper alternative:** add a cheap pre-filter. Count links per child once, using a `BTreeMap&lt;NodeId, u32&gt;` in one O(L) pass. Then only evaluate `inside`, `is_descendant_of(.., root)` and `winning_link` for links whose child has two or more links.
  - A node can only be held if it is dual-linked: the losing ref from inside plus the winning ref from outside.
  - In a well-formed snapshot there are zero such links, so the function drops to O(L log L).
- **Keeps behavior exactly:** yes.
  - A child with a single link whose parent is inside is always inside, cycle guard included. If the parent's chain went through the child, the parent's own walk would hit the cycle guard and return false, which contradicts the parent being inside. So such a child can never pass `!inside(link.child)`.
  - Output order (sort plus dedup by id) is unchanged, and the function is infallible, so there is no error precedence to preserve.
  - A larger rework (one winning-parent map with walks against the map) would also work, but it would restate the `links_ranked` tiebreak, which the `links_ranked` doc comment warns against. The pre-filter avoids that.

**Checked and not worth changing:**

- **`create.rs` `drop_held_refs`:** it scans `held_outside` twice per child (`find`, then `retain`/`any`). `held_outside` is the dual-link residue, almost always empty or tiny. Merging into one `retain` would only save a pass, and the current check-then-mutate order is harmless because the body is discarded on `Err`. Leave as is.
- **`create.rs` `reseal_granted_interior`:** the added `held_outside.iter().any(..)` per frontier node costs O(frontier × held) with held ≈ 0. It also saves work, because a held node is skipped before its `resolve_moving_child` network read.
- **`net/rotation.rs` `promote_scope_root`:** `drop_held_refs` runs on the already-resolved `current.read_body` in place. It adds no extra resolve, decode or clone.
- **No other cost:** `HeldNode` is `Copy` and passed as a slice everywhere, so there are no clones. No new sequential I/O is introduced.</result>

<result>Summary: Standards has 0 hard violations and 5 judgement smells. The worst smell is the three separate decisions about which reason a save can sign over. Spec has 3 findings. The worst is M1: a lapsed record from a newer release can be overwritten.

## Standards

- **Documented rules: clean.** `QueueHoldReason::check` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:723`) is the one mapping. The WASM getter only calls it. The produce path has release-active `Err` checks (`SequenceExhausted`, newer-release refusal) and no `assert!`. I found no tracker refs and no TS enums. The tests check behavior.
- **Repeated Switches (judgement), `crates/engine/src/settings.rs:444`, `:589`, `:602`.** `holds()`, `verified_sequence` and `save_floor` each match the same reasons. The `holds()` doc says "The one place the split is decided", and that is now false. Recommend one `DefaultsReason` method that returns the sequence to sign above or a refusal. Build `holds()` and `save_floor` on it.
- **Mysterious Name (judgement), `settings.rs:602`.** `save_floor` returns an observed sequence, not a floor in the CONTEXT.md sense. Rename it to `sign_above`, and remove the sentence "The floor still rises only on a confirm".
- **Primitive Obsession (judgement), `crates/engine/src/record_plane.rs:439-441`.** `newer_release: bool` copies `Unopened::NewerRelease`. Carry the enum.
- **Readability (judgement), `settings.rs:579-580`.** The code uses the `Option` order (`Some &gt; None`). Use `matches!((h, l), (Some(h), Some(l)) if l &gt; h)`.
- **Middle Man (judgement), `settings.rs:806`.** `publish_settings` only forwards to `publish_settings_above`, and only tests call it.
- **Comments (minor).** The text "which a save must sign above" occurs three times (in `record_plane.rs` near lines 76-86, and in the `save_floor` doc). The comment in `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs` near line 546 repeats its home doc in `drain.rs`. Keep each text once.

## Spec

- **M1, Medium, `record_plane.rs:424`.** I checked this in the code. ADR 0062 D4 says: "When a newer release wrote the body ... the save is refused." But the load returns `Expired { sequence }` before it fetches or opens the body, so `newer_release` is never known. `save_floor` then returns `Ok(Some(seq))`. Failing case: a newer release writes sequence 3, and the record lapses. An older device loads it, takes the hold, and saves at sequence 4. The newer body is lost. Also, `redecide_placement` can move `Unreadable{newer_release:true}` to `Expired{higher}`, and that unlocks the save. Fix: open the body for a lapsed record, or carry `newer_release` on `Expired`. Refuse the save when the release is unknown. Add a test.
- **M2, Medium (partial, not a regression), `record_plane.rs:365`.** If the device has a cached copy, a lapsed record gives `Stale{.., Expired}`. The session is then `Member`, `save_floor` returns `None`, and the save signs at the floor + 1. The read-back sees a higher sequence, so the save never confirms. Fix: keep the verified sequence of the stale reason in the placement.
- **L3, Low, `settings.rs:576`.** A `FloorUnreadable` re-check that times out moves the session to `Assumed(TimedOut)`. After that, only a `Resolved` load re-decides placement. An account that has no record stays refused. Fix: re-decide placement while the load is `TimedOut` or `FloorUnreadable`.
- **Clean:** the sequence comes from `fanout_get_verify` under the account's own name. The floor rises only after `Published`. Both sides of the comparison must hold a verified sequence, and it must be strictly higher. A save that lands clears the hold. Fold items (1) to (4) are present. `fe07303e4` does not change behavior. Nothing is out of scope.

My notes are in `/Users/myankelev/.claude/scratch/w21/LE-settings/review2/notes.txt`.</result>

<result>I found two problems on the grant path and no access-control leak. A held node is never moved into the grantee scope or re-keyed to it.

**(a) Missing or partial requirements**

1. **Medium. Mechanism confirmed, the trigger state is plausible.** Spec: "`converge_grant_subtree` removes held node ids from the unconverged set before it refuses."
   - Where: `crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs:1017` and `crates/engine/src/rotation/sweep.rs:656,681`.
   - Cause: the filter acts after the sweep and covers only the held ids. The sweep still goes into each held node and its subtree.
   - Scenario: a held node X is a scope root in the parent scope's direct index, for example a folder granted earlier that is dual-linked from inside. The sweep puts X in `skipped_scope_roots`. `subtree_child_scopes` leaves X out of `planned`. Then `boundaries != planned` (create.rs:1038) returns `SubtreeBoundaryDiverged` on every retry. This is the same class of failure that 4a799955d fixes.
   - Second scenario: a descendant of a readable held node loses a CAS race or cannot be read. The grant still refuses, because only the held id is filtered.
   - Fix: give the held ids to `converge_subtree` as a stop set, the way `reseal_granted_interior` skips them. Then remove the `retain` filter. Add a test that dual-links a scope root.

**(c) Implemented but wrong**

2. **Low. Plausible.** Spec: "the grant drops a published ref only while it still loses to that winner."
   - Where: `create.rs:1503-1519`.
   - Cause: `drop_held_refs` compares against the snapshot's winner. It does not check that the winner's ref still exists.
   - Scenario: another device removes the outside ref and does not raise the inside one. The grant drops the only ref that is left, and the node is unlinked.
   - Note: I found no honest flow that makes this state, because a move raises the counter and a delete unlinks all refs.
   - Fix: write it down as a known limit, or check that the winner's parent still lists the node before the drop.

**Clean items**

- **Stale re-link and the order of refusals:** clean.
  - A raised inside counter is refused (`link_rank` gives `Greater`).
  - A second inside parent is refused, because each inside ref is compared with the winner.
  - The root promotion refuses before the root publish (`net/rotation.rs:2495`).
  - The interior path refuses before it publishes the parent that holds the ref. Earlier publishes are accepted by the spec: "past the root publish, a retry after a refresh resumes the move".
  - The resume path passes the same `held_outside` through `hand_over_granted_folder`.
- **(b) Scope of a held node:** clean. The sweep re-seals a held node only under `scope_ref`, the parent scope. If the node is in another scope, the read fails and the sweep marks it unreachable. `reseal_granted_interior` skips held ids, so a held node never gets the grantee seed.
- **faccefa18 pre-filter:** clean.
  - A child with one link from an inside parent P has P as its winner. `is_descendant_of(P, node)` is true and has no cycle, so the child is inside.
  - Counting links over the whole snapshot is correct.
  - `filter_map` cannot drop a node, because each child comes from a link, so `winning_link` is `Some`.
- **(d) `link_rank`:** clean. It gives the same tiebreak as before: highest counter, then lowest parent id. `!= Less`, which includes `Equal`, refuses. The `Equal` case cannot occur, because the winner's parent is outside the folder. No other comparator remains.
- **Acceptance tests:** clean. A tie at counter 1 runs for both parent-id orders, with a grant and a soft delete. The grant result is checked against the rank.
- **New tests:** clean. They do not depend on the order of entropy draws, because a created link has counter 1 and the dual link has counter 0.
- **Scope creep:** none.</result>

## Spec

The sub-agent found no access-control leak. A held node never moves into the grantee scope, and it never gets the grantee keys.

1. **MEDIUM. The mechanism is CONFIRMED. The trigger is PLAUSIBLE.** In create.rs at line 1017, `converge_grant_subtree` removes the held ids only after the sweep. The sweep still goes into each held node and its subtree. Two cases fail:
   - (i) Held node X is a scope root that was granted before and is also linked from inside the folder. The sweep puts X in `skipped_scope_roots`. `subtree_child_scopes` (facade.rs:3945) leaves X out of `planned`. Then `boundaries != planned` (create.rs:1038) gives `SubtreeBoundaryDiverged` on every retry. This is the same class of failure that 4a799955d fixes.
   - (ii) A descendant of a held node loses a CAS race or cannot be read. That descendant still refuses the grant.

   Recommended change: give the held ids to `converge_subtree` as a stop set, as `reseal_granted_interior` does. Then remove the `retain`. Add a test that links a scope root from two parents.
2. **LOW, PLAUSIBLE.** `drop_held_refs` compares with the winner from the snapshot. It does not check that the winning ref still exists. If another device removes the outside ref and does not raise the inside ref, the grant drops the last ref, and no folder names the node. The sub-agent found no honest flow that does this. Document the limit, or check that the winning parent still lists the node.

Clean: (a) a stale re-link refuses on both paths, and the root promotion refuses before its publish. The exclusion comes only from `held_outside`, and it uses `link_rank`. Resume passes `held_outside`. (b) The sweep reseals a held node in its own scope only. (c) The pre-filter loses no held node, and the cycle guard holds. (d) `link_rank` keeps the old tiebreak: highest counter, then lowest parent id. The acceptance tests for #2113 are present. There is no scope creep.

**Summary:** Standards has 6 findings. The worst is that a held-ref refusal after the root publish reaches the host as `MalformedInput`, not `PartialCommit`. Spec has 2 findings. The worst is that a held scope root still gives `SubtreeBoundaryDiverged`, because the sweep goes into held nodes.

&gt; **D1 — The name wave opens an interior node below the read-epoch floor, and is the fourth sanctioned reader below that floor.** The arm runs only when the gate refuses the node with `EpochBelowFloor`. It anchors on the scope root that this wave passed through the full root gate, and takes that root's epoch and history links. It opens the node through the child resolve's `open_under_anchor` (one seed walk, ADR 0021 D3). It holds the four conditions of ADR 0021 D2: the record carries no grant section, the read moves no read-epoch floor, the sequence bar is the replay bar, and the epoch is one that the anchor's ratchet reaches and is below the anchor's epoch. Every other refusal still stops the wave.

**Alternatives text**
&gt; - **Sweep the scope to convergence before the write cut.** Each node then publishes twice, once for the sweep and once for the wave. The sweep isolates a node that it cannot reach and goes on, so it does not prove convergence, and a node that lags again between the two passes still stops the wave.
&gt; - **Cut the write plane before the read plane in `rotate_on_cut`.** Then no child lags during a revoke. But a write grant or a downgrade after a read rotation still meets lagging nodes, so this fixes only part of the problem.</result>

## Spec

**F1, Medium, CONFIRMED (`settings.rs:488-493`). A lapsed body that does not open stops all saves, with no exit.**
- `Expired { unopened: Some(Malformed) }` gives `Refused`. But `Unreadable { Malformed }` gives `Clears`.
- ADR 0062 D4 says: "The same rule holds when the load reports `Expired` or `Unreadable`".
- Scenario: a corrupt body at sequence 3 lapses. Each save is refused. No hold occurs, and no renewal or `Resolved` result arrives. The account can never save settings again.
- Fix: map `Expired + Malformed` to `Clears { observed: Some(sequence) }`. Refuse only `NewerRelease` and `Unavailable`. Add a `write_plane` test for this case.

**F2, Low, CONFIRMED (`settings.rs:640-655`). A head-fetch failure stops saves until the app restarts.**
- A held `Expired { Unavailable }` gives `observed() == None`. A later re-check that gives `Expired { None }` at the same sequence does not pass `newer_verified`, and it is not `unsettled`.
- Fix: add this reason to `unsettled`.

**F3, Low.** Only the pure-function test (about `settings.rs:1906`) covers L3. No `write_plane` test covers it. The M1 and M2 tests (`write_plane.rs:14270`, `:14313`) test behavior.

  - The CID comes from the verified record, and `read_block` checks the block against it.

<result>PR #2165 should not merge yet: I found three confirmed high-severity defects. I confirmed each finding by tracing the code at head `1f810df8`. I did not build the code or run a probe, and I wrote no notes to the scratch directory.

## High

**H1. A revoke or a downgrade of a different recipient can return `Ok` and do nothing.** CONFIRMED.
- Where: `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, `revoke_grant` (about line 7019) and `change_permission` (about line 8098).
- Mechanism: both functions return `Ok(())` when `redrive_scope` returns `StillOwed`. They do not check which recipient the command names. `redrive_scope` also returns `StillOwed`, with no event, when a sync pass holds `Running`.
- Scenario 1: the owner revokes Alice and the wave stops. The owner then revokes Bob at the same scope. The command returns `Ok`, but Bob keeps his grant.
- Scenario 2: a grant to Alice owes its delivery, and the owner revokes Alice. The revoke returns `Ok`, and a later pass then delivers the grant to Alice.
- Fix: when `StillOwed`, return `Ok` only if the recipient has no row. Otherwise, return a retryable `Err` such as "rotation work owed".

**H2. Another cut or grant at the same scope replaces the owed entry, so the owed work is lost.** CONFIRMED.
- Where: `OwedRotation::owe` (`crates/engine/src/sync/owed_rotation.rs`, `record.insert`), `rotate_owed_cut`, and the mint path of `share_scope`.
- Mechanism: `revoke_link` and the expired-link sweep (`link_sweep.rs`) call `rotate_owed_cut`, and it calls `owe` first. Neither path re-drives first.
- Scenario: the wave of Alice's write revoke stops. The PR notes that this always occurs today for a scope with a child node, because of the #2153 defect. A link revoke or an expired-link sweep then writes `{N+1, [ReadCut]}` over the entry and clears it. The `WriteCut` step is gone, and Alice keeps the write seed for ever with no event.
- The same loss occurs when the cut set publish is refused (`Some(false)` → `clear`) or when it is unknown (`None` → the entry is replaced).
- It also occurs in `share_scope`: a share to recipient B while A's stalled mint stands goes to the mint path. `create_grant` returns `ResumeNotThisGrant`, which is a pre-publish error, so `clear(node)` erases A's owed delivery and write cut.
- A tick that re-drives at the same time as a command can also `clear` the entry that the command just wrote.
- Fix: when an entry stands, refuse with a retryable `Err` before the publish (for the sweep, skip the scope on this pass). Or merge the steps and clear only the steps that the command added.

**H3. A downgrade whose cut-set publish result is unknown can make the scope unusable on the owner's device.** CONFIRMED.
- Where: `redrive_write_cut` and `redrive_entry` (`facade/owed_rotation.rs`).
- Mechanism: a downgrade is a write-only cut, so its entry is `[WriteCut]` with no `ReadCut` step. Only `ReadCut` checks `commitment.cut_epoch &lt; cut_epoch`.
- Scenario: the `publish_cut_set` call fails and the read-back also fails (`None`), so the entry stays at cut epoch N. The next pass runs a wave over the set that was not cut, so B is still a writer and gets the new write seed. The pass then calls `record_cut_epoch_floor(N)`. The published commitment is at N-1, so the gate (`refuse_stale_cut_epoch`) refuses every later resolve of the scope on this device. A retry of the downgrade also fails.
- Fix: in `redrive_entry`, before any step, if `cut_epoch &gt; 0` and the published cut epoch is below it, clear the entry and raise no floor. Add a test for this.

## Medium

**M1. A grant can return `Done` but never mint.** CONFIRMED.
- Mechanism: `OwedRotation::store` writes the cell before `put_staged_bytes`. A D2 refusal therefore leaves the entry in the session cell, and D5 says it must leave no entry.
- Scenario: a retry of the same grant before the next pass sees `DeliverGrant`. The re-drive finds no promoted root, so it returns `NothingOwed`, which becomes `Finished`. `share_scope` then vouches the contact and returns `Done`, but no grant exists.
- The D2 tests check only events, not the cell.
- Fix: write the cell only after the store accepts the write, or roll the cell back in `owe`. Do not treat `NothingOwed` as `Finished` in `share_scope`.

**M2. An entry that can never land stays for ever.** CONFIRMED.
- Examples: the folder was deleted (`owed-scope-not-indexed`), the folder was moved (`owed-interior-move-source-moved`), or the contact was removed (`owed-grant-recipient-unknown`).
- Each pass re-drives these entries and sends an event, and nothing can drop them.
- At 64 such entries, every revoke and every grant refuses with `owed-rotation-record-full`.
- Fix: drop or park an entry after a terminal refusal on a scope that is gone, and send one final event.

**M3. The ADR 0020 two-step landing is not met.** CONFIRMED.
- #2159 is still open and no release contains it (the latest release is v2.8.0). This PR carries both the prefix and the first write.
- Consequence 7 needs a release with #2159 before this PR merges.

**M4. Deviation (1) is not in the docs.**
- ADR 0063 D1, `CONTEXT.md` "Owed rotation work" and `blueprint/engine.md` still say "a write grant".
- Fix: amend them in this PR.

## Plausible

**P1. The "landed" branch of `redrive_write_cut` trusts an epoch from the wire.**
- Mechanism: it accepts `current.write_epoch &gt;= write_epoch` from the resolved root and raises the floor with it. `floor.rs` states "never one it read off the wire".
- Scenario: if the gate admits a root that the revoked writer published at the old name with an inflated `write_epoch`, the re-drive clears the entry with no wave.
- Fix: accept "landed" only when `moved_root` (the owner-signed pointer) placed the target.

**P2. A parent-scope writer can make the re-drive drop a stalled grant.**
- Mechanism: the writer publishes a record at the folder name with no grant section. `promoted_root` then answers "not promoted", and the re-drive clears the whole entry.

**P3. A read cut can run twice.**
- Mechanism: `redrive_read_cut` cannot see that a read cut already landed when its `advance_to` was lost at a restart. It runs a second read cascade, which breaks the D1 rule that a re-drive cuts nothing again.

**P4. D4 reads the stored record, not the session cell.**
- After a refused store write, the walk can renew names of a scope that this session owes.

## Gates

- **`/code-review` (standards): clean.** The comments are short, with no tracker references.
- **`/code-review` (spec):** H1–H3, M1–M4.
- **`/security-review`:** H1, H2, M2, P1, P2.
- **`/crypto-privacy-review`:**
  - (a) Clean. An entry holds only ids, epochs, a recipient public identity key and a flag. The staging key is `owner_scoped_key`, the AEAD binds `OwedRotation` 0x0a, and there are 16 new cross-kind rejects (82 in total).
  - (b) Clean. The encoder refuses every shape the decoder refuses, the checks are release-active, and CI runs `--release --test encode_refusals`.
  - (c) Clean on all four paths: the entry is written before the first publish.
  - (d) Fails: M1, H3.
  - (e) The wave keeps `recover_wave` and refuses another epoch. Every read goes through `resolve_anchored`. P1 and P3 remain.
  - (f) Clean apart from P4.
  - (g) The re-drive is bounded per pass, and the delivery goes to the stored recipient. H2, P1 and P2 remain.
  - (h) Deviation (1) is safe and it is needed: under D5 a read grant whose interior move stops returns `Ok`, so without an owed delivery the share pointer is lost.</result>

<result>The review found one confirmed problem with `locate_miss`, two plausible issues, and four of the five checks came out clean.

**(c) Implemented but wrong**

1. **CONFIRMED: a route that failed once on the network is never retried.** Spec (fold 4): "`locate_miss` remembers a target the walk did not find until the base changes." In the code, "base" is only the link count, `snapshot.links().len()` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:8924-8927`, `:8960-8963`). The miss is also recorded when a leg fails for a temporary reason such as an unavailable or timed-out record.
   - Mechanism: `settle_focus_leg` stamps every folder it tried, even a failed one, so nothing is added to the base. The miss stands until some other change alters the link count. The tick never lists the parents below a focus it does not hold, so that may not happen.
   - Failing scenario: the leader tab's route to `/files/X` hits the slow record plane described in #2147/#2152, and the miss is recorded. A follower tab then reloads `/files/X`. The leader engine is still alive, so the follower's route skips the walk and shows `unknown node` again. A refocus or back/forward navigation in the same tab does the same.
   - Fix: record the miss only when every leg in the walk answered. Or store the time of the miss and let it expire with `refresh_due(Some(at), now, profile)`.

**(a) Missing or partial**

2. **PLAUSIBLE: the staging budget.** Spec #2152: "The staging scenario should also use a navigation budget appropriate for the deployed record plane." Fold 6 keeps the default budget for `toRoot()` (`tests/web-e2e/staging/workspace.spec.ts:57`), which is safe only if the cached view paints right away. `async_lock::RwLock` makes new readers wait behind a queued writer. So any command queued while a route holds the read lock blocks the root `snapshot` until the route finishes.

3. **PLAUSIBLE: the 10 s bound is narrower than the lock it protects.** `LOCATE_WALK_WAIT` limits only the wait for the walk (`facade.rs:8983`). The locate legs that follow run under the read lock with no overall limit. They are capped only by `MAX_LOCATE_FOLDERS` (256 folders) and by each resolve's own budget. A logout or forget, which needs the write lock, waits up to 10 s plus those legs. Two related points:
   - A walk rejected in the middle of a wait does not wake the waiters, so the route sits out the rest of the 10 s.
   - Suggested fix: `within(LOCATE_WALK_WAIT, …)` around all of `locate_folder`, and a wake from the rejection branch at `sync/pass.rs:605`.

**(b) Scope creep:** none. Taking the read lock for `ManualRefresh` in `crates/wasm/src/host.rs:227-236` falls under #2152's write-lock concern. The guard is released before `landed()` is awaited.

**Clean checks**

- **Lost wake:** none. The check of `boundary_walk_landed`, the `boundary_walk_landing()` registration and `file_forced_pass()` run with no await between them, and a `send` before the first poll stays buffered. With no sync loop running, both `Ok(None)` and `Err` return before any wait. A walk already rejected returns before registration.
- **Teardown and waiter leaks:** none. A logout replaces the engine, so its `SessionState` drops, the senders drop and receivers get `Canceled`. A route that times out leaves a cancelled sender, which `retain(!is_canceled)` removes at the next registration. The tick loop runs through `spawn_local` outside the RwLock, so a walk can land while a route holds the read lock.
- **`refresh_due` at the four sites:** all match the old expressions exactly.
  - `tick.rs` `focus_folders_due`: `get().copied()` gives the same result as the old `is_none_or`.
  - `received_status.rs`: `.map(|h| h.at)` gives the same result.
  - `facade.rs:11353` focus hint: `last` is still `stamp.max(hint)`, and `None` is still due.
  - `locate_folder`: a new site.
  - The `&gt;=` boundary is still inside `elapsed_at_least`.
- **Fold 3:** `set_focus` calls `scheduler.now()` after `locate_folder` has finished.
- **`clearStore`:** every path still clears the email and the Core Kit secret. `purge` sits in a `finally`, and `logout` calls `clearStore` in its own `finally`. If `removeItem` throws, the email that remains is sealed under the wrapping key `purge` deletes, so it can no longer be read.</result>

<summary>Agent "Simplify efficiency review" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I found five efficiency issues in PR #2165, and none of them is serious. Only finding 1 adds real network cost. Line numbers are from the worktree.

**1. Repeated network read of the scope in a cut re-drive**
- **File:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adbf0d4266bd305fe/crates/engine/src/facade/owed_rotation.rs`, lines 366-409 (`redrive_entry`), with the reads at 373, 567 and 605.
- **Summary:** For a cut entry (`cut_epoch &gt; 0`), `redrive_entry` calls `owed_scope` to check the cut epoch. Then the first step (`redrive_read_cut` or `redrive_write_cut`) calls `owed_scope` again for the same scope. Nothing is published between the two calls.
- **Cost:** Each `owed_scope` call does three network reads: the parent index resolve, the scope-pointer read (`moved_root`, a fan-out GET) and the gated root resolve. A revoke entry `[ReadCut, WriteCut]` therefore does nine reads, and three of them repeat. This occurs on each pass and each command re-drive while the entry stands.
- **Cheaper form:** Keep the `OwedScope` from the epoch check in an `Option`. Give it to the first step with `.take()`, and let each later step read again. The first step still gets a gated, pointer-placed result, so no check goes away. The only difference: a remote publish in the gap between the two reads is no longer seen.
- **Confidence:** Medium-high.

**2. `OwedRotation::entry` clones the whole record to return one entry**
- **File:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adbf0d4266bd305fe/crates/engine/src/sync/owed_rotation.rs`, lines 207-226 (`load`, `entry`).
- **Summary:** `entry()` calls `load()`, which clones the whole `BTreeMap` (up to 64 entries, each with a `Vec` of steps). Then it keeps one entry and drops the rest.
- **Cost:** The callers that make this matter:
  - `redrive_owed` (`facade/owed_rotation.rs` line 319) clones the map once, then calls `entry()` once per scope. That is O(n²) entry clones on every tick that holds an entry.
  - `link_sweep.rs` line 243 calls `entry()` once per swept scope.
  - The command paths `owed_entry`, `redrive_owed_at` and `clear_owed_move` each clone the full map.
- **Cheaper form:** In `entry()`, when the cell is loaded, borrow it and return `record.get(&amp;scope).cloned()`. Use `load()` only for a cold read. For `redrive_owed` and `owed_scopes` (`renewal_walk.rs` line 443), add a method that returns only the scope keys. Do not change the mutating methods: their clone-then-store keeps the order "store before cell".
- **Confidence:** High that the waste exists. Low cost in absolute terms, because the record holds at most 64 entries.

**3. The write-name derivation runs twice for each dark descendant scope**
- **File:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adbf0d4266bd305fe/crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs`, line 1398 (the new `write_cut_unfinished`) and line 1450 (`write_plane`).
- **Summary:** `write_plane` already calls `seed_names` on the gated `write_scope_seed`. When the write plane fails, the new code calls `seed_names` on the same seed again.
- **Cost:** One `derive_write_name` per dark descendant scope per boundary walk. That is a BLAKE3 derivation, an Ed25519 public-key derivation and an IPNS name build, which costs more in WASM.
- **Cheaper form:** Compute `gated.write_scope_seed.as_ref().map(|s| seed_names(s, &amp;scope_id, Some(name)))` once in the caller. Give the bool to `write_plane`, or let `write_plane` return it. The result is the same.
- **Confidence:** High that it is a duplicate, low impact.

**4. Owner commands build the pass and its keys three or four times**
- **File:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adbf0d4266bd305fe/crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, lines 7040-7041, 7153, 7480-7496, 7634, 7865 and 7878.
- **Summary:** Each helper calls `pass_keys(session)` and `conversion_pass(...)` on its own:
  - Revoke: `cancel_owed_delivery`, then `redrive_owed_at`, then sometimes `owed_cut_stands`, which calls `owed_entry`.
  - Grant: `owed_entry`, then `redrive_owed_at`, then `keys_for_pass`.
  - Permission change: `redrive_owed_at`, then `owed_cut_stands`.
- **Cost:** `pass_keys` does `owner_identity()`, which is a secp256k1 `verifying_key()` point multiplication. It also does an `Rc` clone of the sweep factory and a map clone (see finding 2). Each command repeats this three or four times.
- **Cheaper form:** Build `PassKeys` and the `ConversionPass` once per command, and give the pass to the helpers. Each helper still takes its own `OwedCell::hold` exactly where it does now.
- **Confidence:** Medium. The cost is small.

**5. The grant path reads the entry and then re-drives, which reads it again**
- **File:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adbf0d4266bd305fe/crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, lines 7480-7496.
- **Summary:** `owed_entry(node)` reads the entry outside the hold to test for `DeliverGrant`. Then `redrive_owed_at(node)` reads the same entry again under the hold.
- **Cost:** One extra pass construction and one extra full-map clone per contact grant.
- **Cheaper form:** Let `redrive_scope` also return the `OwedEntry` it read under the hold, and compute `owed_delivery` from that. This also removes finding 4's extra pass for the grant. With one driver, the behavior is the same. When the pass runs at the same time, the read moves inside the hold: the hold refuses the command or the entry is re-read, which is the stricter form.
- **Confidence:** Medium-low. Merge this with finding 4.

**Checked and not flagged:**
- `unfinished_write_cuts.borrow().clone()` in the liveness loop (`facade.rs`, around line 6069): the clone is needed. A borrow held across the `.await` would panic when `sync/pass.rs` writes the set with `borrow_mut`.
- The two resolves of the parent in `redrive_interior_move`: the second, in `probe_promotion`, is the freshness proof behind `ParentScopeSuperseded`. Removing it would weaken a check.
- `owed_scope` in `redrive_delivery` after a write step: the gate on the new root must run, so the new name cannot be reused.
- Owed-record writes do not bump the staging generation (`QueueGenerationStore::put_staged_bytes` does not count them), so they do not invalidate the render memo.
- `redrive_owed` on a tick with no entries: one cached clone of an empty map, so the cost is negligible. Its order with `conversion.run` is sequential because both take the `Running` latch.
- The `apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.ts` change only adds three `warn` branches and costs nothing.</result>

<result>I found eight simplifications and one comment defect. None of them changes behavior, a check, an error class, a wire byte, the store-before-cell order or `OwedCell::hold`. Line numbers are worktree lines where I checked them (Fn), otherwise diff lines (Dn).

1. **`crates/engine/src/facade/owed_rotation.rs`, enum `Settled` and `settle_redrive`** (D1422-1428, D1525-1541, D1700-1743).
   - Summary: `Settled::NeverLanded` copies the terminal-stop path.
   - Cost: one extra private enum and one extra match arm. `settle_redrive` has two arms that both call `abandon` and return `Redriven::Dropped`.
   - Simpler form: in `redrive_entry`, return `Err(OwedStop::abandoned(OWED_CUT_NEVER_LANDED))` in place of `Ok(Settled::NeverLanded)`. Change the return type to `Result&lt;(), OwedStop&gt;` and delete `Settled`. The `Err(stop) if stop.terminal` arm then gives the same `abandon(scope, "owed-cut-never-landed")` and `Dropped`. The event detail does not change.
   - Confidence: high.

2. **`facade/owed_rotation.rs`, `redrive_owed` against `redrive_scope`** (D1653-1695).
   - Summary: the loop body is a second copy of `redrive_scope`.
   - Cost: two copies of the sequence "hold, read the entry again, `redrive_entry`, `settle_redrive`". They can drift apart.
   - Simpler form: `for scope in record.into_keys() { let _ = self.redrive_scope(sites, scope).await; }`. A refused hold, a failed entry read and `NoEntry` each do the same as the current `continue`. The `Running` guard stays at the top of `redrive_owed`.
   - Confidence: high.

3. **`crates/engine/src/sync/owed_rotation.rs`, `OwedStep::check()`** (F86-92). The step-name literals are at `facade/owed_rotation.rs` F46, F474, F564, F599 and F658.
   - Summary: `OwedStep::check()` is dead code. Nothing in `crates/` calls it. Five places spell the same four strings by hand: `"owed-interior-move"`, `"owed-read-cut"`, `"owed-write-cut"` (twice, once in `of_post_step`) and `"owed-grant-delivery"`.
   - Cost: two sources for the same names. Also one public method with no caller.
   - Simpler form: delete `OwedStep::check()`. Or make `OwedStop::of` take `&amp;OwedStep` and call `step.check()`, which removes the literals. The detail strings do not change.
   - Confidence: high that it is dead. Medium on which form to pick.

4. **`crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, `drive_cut`** (F7285-7340, D707-759).
   - Summary: the function matches on `owes` three times: once for `_hold`, once for the rotate call, and once more with `owes.is_some()` before the clear. It also builds the owed `WriteCut` step a second time with `saturating_add(1)`. `rotate_owed_cut` already builds that step with `checked_add(1)` (D1563-1566).
   - Cost: branching that is hard to follow, and one step value built in two places with different overflow arithmetic.
   - Simpler form:
     - Write the hold as `let _hold = owes.map(|_| self.state.owed_rotation.hold(node).ok_or_else(EngineError::rotation_work_owed)).transpose()?;`.
     - Keep one `match owes` for the rotate.
     - Have `rotate_owed_cut` return the `WriteCut` step it built, or add one `fn owed_write_cut(write_epoch) -&gt; Result&lt;OwedStep, EngineError&gt;`. `drive_cut` then uses that step and does not build it again. The `checked_add` already succeeded at that point, so behavior is the same.
   - Confidence: medium.

5. **`facade.rs`, the write arm of the share mint** (D952-978).
   - Summary: `match self.resolve_owned_scope(..).await { Ok(m) =&gt; self.moved_by_write_cut(..).await, Err(e) =&gt; Err(e) }` writes the `?` operator out by hand. A second `and_then` follows it.
   - Cost: two nested matches for a chain of three fallible steps.
   - Simpler form: `let named = async { let minted = self.resolve_owned_scope(..).await?; let moved = self.moved_by_write_cut(node, &amp;minted.target, &amp;minted.current).await?; parsed_scope_name(&amp;moved.scope.ipns_name) }.await;`, then one `match named { Ok(name) =&gt; .., Err(e) =&gt; stop_owed .. }`.
   - Confidence: high.

6. **`facade.rs`, the advance of `owed_steps` in the share mint** (D942-943, D969-970).
   - Summary: the pair "`let mut owed_steps = owed_steps.split_off(1)`, then `advance_to(node, &amp;owed_steps[0])`" occurs twice. The first time also shadows the variable.
   - Cost: two copies, and `split_off` reads as "keep the tail", which is not obvious.
   - Simpler form: `owed_steps.remove(0); let _ = pass.owed().advance_to(node, &amp;owed_steps[0]).await;`. You can also put this in a small closure or helper that you call twice.
   - Confidence: medium.

7. **`facade.rs`, the new owed wrappers `cancel_owed_delivery`, `clear_owed_move`, `owed_entry` and `redrive_owed_at`** (D634-653, D1015-1063).
   - Summary: four copies of the setup "session, api, `pass_keys`, `conversion_pass`". Two of them also take the hold. `revoke` calls `cancel_owed_delivery` and then `redrive_owed_at`, so it builds two passes in sequence.
   - Cost: about 16 copied lines in a hot file.
   - Simpler form: move `cancel_delivery`-under-hold and `clear_owed_move` onto `ConversionPass` in `facade/owed_rotation.rs`, next to `redrive_scope`, which already takes its own hold. Each facade command then builds one pass and calls pass methods.
   - Confidence: medium. The local borrow of `keys` makes one shared helper awkward, so the move is the cheaper form.

8. **`facade/owed_rotation.rs`, `OwedStop::of`** (D1360-1376).
   - Summary: `terminal` uses a second `matches!` on the same `error`.
   - Cost: two matches on one value.
   - Simpler form: put the terminal case in the first match, `UnsupportedTarget { check } if *check == OWED_SCOPE_NOT_INDEXED =&gt; (*check, false, true)`, and return a three-value tuple. `cut_stop` and `of_grant` can also use `OwedStop { retryable: .., ..OwedStop::refused(check) }`, as `OWED_MOVE_NOT_PROMOTED` already does.
   - Confidence: low, because the gain is small.

9. **`sync/owed_rotation.rs`, the test module** (D3000-3004).
   - Summary: this is a comment defect. The doc line "What one session sealed is what the next one re-drives." sits above `a_held_scope_refuses_a_second_driver_until_the_first_drops`. It belongs to `a_sealed_record_opens_as_the_entries_it_named`, which has no doc.
   - Cost: the hold test now shows two unrelated doc paragraphs, and the comment is false where it sits.
   - Simpler form: move that line to `a_sealed_record_opens_as_the_entries_it_named`.
   - Confidence: high.

Smaller items, all low confidence:

- **`crates/engine/src/net/renewal_walk.rs` D2311:** `owed.as_ref().map_or_else(|_| Vec::new(), |owed| ..)` can be `owed.as_ref().map(|owed| ..).unwrap_or_default()`.
- **`renewal_walk.rs` `owed_scopes` (D2359-2364):** it builds `OwedRotation { .. }` by hand, the same way `ConversionPass::owed()` does. A small `OwedRotation::new(staging, seal, enc_secret, cell)` would remove the copy.
- **`facade/owed_rotation.rs` D1966:** `"owed-write-cut-ran-no-wave"` is an inline literal, but every other re-drive check is a named `const`. Make it a const, for consistency.
- **`crates/engine/tests/owner_actions.rs` D4386-4393:** the `WriteCutUnfinished` filter-and-dedup copies the shape of `owed_scopes` and `abandoned`. One generic `reported(events, pick)` helper would serve all three, and the assertions stay the same.

I found no comment that breaks the AGENTS.md rules (absence-justifying text, apologia for unchanged code, bare tracker references, or an oversized module header), apart from the misplaced doc line in item 9. I found no redundant session state: `owed_rotation_driven` and `scope_roots_walked` are set by different legs, so neither is derivable from the other.</result>

<result>I found seven altitude findings. Two of them are strong: findings 1 and 2. The worst pattern is that one D5 rule ("the same command re-drives its own entry") is coded by hand in three commands, and two of those copies have the same truth table. Line numbers are in the worktree at `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-adbf0d4266bd305fe`.

**1. `crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs:458` (`is_post_publish`), used at `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:7683`**
- **Summary:** The contact share finds out whether its promotion published by matching a list of nine error variants. The link share finds out from structure (`InviteMintOutcome::stalled`, filled from `PromotedGrant::handover`).
- **Cost:** There are two ways to answer one question. The variant list must stay in step with the order of steps in `hand_over_granted_folder`. A new handover variant that nobody adds to the list makes a post-publish stop return `Err`, and that drops the entry.
- **Deeper change:** Make `create_grant` return the split that `promote_grantee_scope` already makes: `read_scope` plus `handover: Result&lt;..&gt;`. `resume_grantee_scope` returns it too, with its errors before the handover staying in the outer `Err`. The facade then reads "stalled" the same way for both kinds of share, and `is_post_publish` goes away.
- **Same behaviour?** Yes. I checked that every variant in the list is built only inside `hand_over_granted_folder` / `reseal_granted_interior` (`create.rs` 1392–1628). Errors before the root publishes (`RecipientIsTheOwner`, `UnusableRecipientKey`, `Converge`, `Publish`, `ResumeNotThisGrant`) are not in the list.
- **Inside the diff?** Mostly. It also changes the signature of `create_grant`, which has one production caller (`facade.rs:7671`) and some test callers in `create.rs`.
- **Confidence:** Medium-high.

**2. `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:7273` (`drive_cut`, parameter `owes: Option&lt;u64&gt;`)**
- **Summary:** One flag parameter joins two functions. The code branches on `owes` twice (for the hold and for the report), and the return type becomes `Option&lt;CutRotationReport&gt;` for both callers.
- **Cost:** The caller without an entry (`moved_by_write_cut`, `facade.rs:8419`) must handle an `Ok(None)` that it can never get. It does this with `.and_then(|report| report.write)`, so the impossible case reads as the TrustViolation "reported no name wave".
- **Deeper change:** Split it in two:
  - `drive_owed_cut(.., write_epoch)` for `cut_at`. It takes the hold, calls `rotate_owed_cut` and handles the owed post-step.
  - `drive_cut` for `moved_by_write_cut`. It returns `CutRotationReport` as before.
- **Same behaviour?** Yes.
- **Inside the diff?** Yes.
- **Confidence:** High.

**3. `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:7072` and 7134–7146 (revoke), 8204–8230 (`change_permission`), 7496–7509 (share)**
- **Summary:** Each command codes the D5 "same command re-drives" mapping on its own. Revoke and change_permission have the same truth table:

  | Re-drive result | Own change already shows? | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | StillOwed | yes | `owed_cut_stands` |
  | StillOwed | no | `rotation_work_owed` |
  | Finished | yes | `Ok` |
  | NoEntry or Dropped | — | the original result |

  Each finds "already shows" in its own way. Revoke uses a `still_owed` flag inside its closure and then matches `NotGranted`. Change_permission does a `held_grantee` pre-check and then matches `SamePermission`. Share has a third version (`owed_delivery`, `clear_owed_move`).
- **Cost:** The ADR rule lives in three places. Also, `owed_cut_stands` reads the entry from the store a second time, because `Redriven::StillOwed` drops what the re-drive already knew.
- **Deeper change:** One helper over `(Redriven, own_change_shows: bool)` that gives Proceed / Done / Stands / Refuse. Revoke and change_permission call it. Separately, `Redriven::StillOwed` could carry `is_cut`, which removes `owed_cut_stands` and its read.
- **Same behaviour?** The helper keeps behaviour identical. Carrying `is_cut` is identical except in a race with the tick, where the value read under the hold wins. Treat that part as optional.
- **Inside the diff?** Yes.
- **Confidence:** Medium.

**4. `crates/engine/src/facade/owed_rotation.rs:219` (`rotate_owed_cut`) with `facade.rs:7327–7341` and `facade/link_sweep.rs:278`**
- **Summary:** Three owners share one entry's lifecycle:
  - `rotate_owed_cut` clears an entry for a read-only cut.
  - `drive_cut` clears an entry for a write cut after `after_write_wave`.
  - `link_sweep` never clears an entry for a write cut. It leaves it for the next pass's `redrive_write_cut`.

  The doc comment of `rotate_owed_cut` has to explain this split. The owed `WriteCut` epoch is also computed twice for the same cut (`checked_add(1)` at `owed_rotation.rs:231`, `saturating_add(1)` at `facade.rs:7331`).
- **Cost:** Each caller of `rotate_owed_cut` must know when to clear. The epoch arithmetic can drift.
- **Deeper change:** `rotate_owed_cut` returns the `WriteCut` step it owed, or takes the post-step as an async closure, and then owns stop and clear in one place. `link_sweep` must keep what it does now (its write entry finishes on the next pass), so pass it something that leaves the entry.
- **Same behaviour?** Yes, if `link_sweep` keeps its current behaviour.
- **Inside the diff?** Yes.
- **Confidence:** Medium.

**5. `crates/engine/src/sync/owed_rotation.rs:242` (`leave`) and 278 (`advance_to`), `facade.rs:7787` and 7808 (`split_off(1)`, `[0]`)**
- **Summary:** There are two ways to advance the record. Every call to `leave` (through `stop_owed`) passes a suffix of the stored steps, so `leave` is an advance. The share code advances by position (`split_off(1)`, then `&amp;owed_steps[0]`), which depends on how the list was built further up.
- **Cost:** There are two primitives for one operation, and the positional indexing is fragile. On a stop after the mint, and on the stalled-link path, `leave` writes the same steps again for no reason.
- **Deeper change:** Use one primitive, `advance_past(scope, landed rank)`. It covers the empty-steps case "only the cut-epoch floor is owed". `stop_owed` then takes the step that last landed.
- **Same behaviour?** Yes, apart from losing those redundant writes of identical content.
- **Inside the diff?** Yes.
- **Confidence:** Medium-low.

**6. `crates/engine/src/rotation/trigger.rs:626` (`owed_read_cut`)**
- **Summary:** It builds a write-scope cut and then overwrites `planes`.
- **Cost:** A function named for the write plane is a hidden dependency of the read re-drive.
- **Deeper change:** Add one private `verified_published_cut(plan, planes)`. Both `cut_for_write_scope` and `owed_read_cut` call it.
- **Same behaviour?** Yes.
- **Inside the diff?** Yes.
- **Confidence:** High, but the value is low.

**7. `crates/engine/src/net/renewal_walk.rs:463` and 637**
- **Summary:** The D4 owed-scope filter is applied at two lookup sites (`material` and the bin `find`).
- **Cost:** A third root kind would need its own copy of the check.
- **Deeper change:** One `Pass::skips(scope_id)` predicate. I did not suggest filtering `scopes` and `bins` up front, because that clones `WalkScope` seeds.
- **Same behaviour?** Yes.
- **Inside the diff?** Yes.
- **Confidence:** Low-medium, and the value is low.

**Considered and rejected:**
- **Running the re-drive in `cut_and_rotate` as one gate.** "Own change shows" depends on the command. Link revoke correctly refuses through `OwedRecordError::Standing`.
- **Detecting an unfinished write cut in the renewal walk's own seed filter, without passing `unfinished_write_cuts` through session state.** It changes when the event is sent and which scopes it covers, because the walk is budgeted and held.
- **Holding the scope once for the whole command.** Revoke now takes and drops the hold three times. One hold would change who wins a race with the tick, so it is not the same behaviour.
- **Moving the terminal special case in `OwedStop::of` for `OWED_SCOPE_NOT_INDEXED` to its producer.** It changes the event `detail` string.

I made no edits and no git writes.</result>

**Applied:**
1. **Owed record reads.** A new private `read` helper looks at the cell in place. `entry` now copies one entry, not the full record. A new `scopes()` gives the scope keys to the sync-pass re-drive and to the renewal walk. The write methods still copy the record and then store it, so "store before cell" stays.
2. **Sync-pass re-drive.** `redrive_owed` now calls `redrive_scope` for each scope. The old loop body was a copy of that function.
3. **`Settled` enum removed.** A cut that never landed now returns the terminal stop `OWED_CUT_NEVER_LANDED`. It drops the entry and sends the same event detail.
4. **One fewer network read.** The first owed step uses the scope that the cut-epoch check read. Nothing publishes between the check and that step. Later steps read the scope again.
5. **`drive_cut` split.** `drive_cut` returns `CutRotationReport` again. The new `drive_owed_cut` holds the owed-entry path. One function, `owed_write_cut`, now calculates the `WriteCut` epoch. Before, `checked_add` and `saturating_add` both did it. The value is the same because the post-step runs only after `checked_add` succeeds.
6. **Fewer conversion-pass builds.** The hold, cancel-delivery, clear-move and cut-stands helpers moved onto `ConversionPass`, next to `redrive_scope`. Revoke, share and permission change now build one pass each, not three or four. One `hold_owed` replaces five copies of the hold-or-refuse code. The four old helpers on `Engine` are gone.
7. **One rule for "the change already shows".** Revoke and permission change both use the new `settle_shown`. The outcomes are the same as before.
8. **Share command.** `owed_steps.remove(0)` replaces `split_off(1)` in two places. One async block replaces the hand-written `?` match.
9. **Smaller tidies:**
   - The code uses the core constant `IDENTITY_PUBLIC_LEN`.
   - The unused `OwedStep::check` is removed. I removed it and did not connect it to the step functions, because two of the stop names are not step names.
   - The no-wave check is now the constant `OWED_WAVE_NOT_RUN`.
   - The two re-drive cut plans share one `published_cut_plan` helper.
   - A doc line in the tests moved to the test that it describes.
   - `map(..).unwrap_or_default()` replaces `map_or_else` in the renewal walk.

**Not applied:**
- **The share entry read under the hold.** This needs `redrive_scope` to return the entry, so `Redriven` must carry data. It is a `Copy` enum that the code compares with `==` in many places, so this is not a clean refactor.

2. `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`:3791, `parent_scope_plan`. The fold dropped the `prev: None` reason ("metadata-only re-seal at the same epoch, so it cuts no read plane and mints no history link"). That is real domain reasoning, and now nothing records it. **Fix:** put it back on the `prev` field.
3. `crates/engine/src/facade/owed_rotation.rs`, the `redrive_read_cut` comment ("a re-drive after a lost advance runs one more cascade"). This is a known gap, not a reason for the code. **Fix:** cut it to one line, or move it to ADR 0063 Consequences.

**(b) Judgement calls (smells)**
4. **Possible Primitive Obsession, Medium** (`facade/owed_rotation.rs`:39 and :533). Whether an owed entry is dropped for good is recovered by string-matching `OWED_SCOPE_NOT_INDEXED` inside an `EngineError::UnsupportedTarget`. Any other site that raises that check would silently drop owed work. **Fix:** have `indexed_place` return `OwedStop::abandoned` directly, or add a typed variant.
5. **Possible Duplicated Code, Medium** (`facade.rs`:7083, :7493, :8120). Removing `redrive_owed_at` inlined the same pass-keys, conversion-pass and sites setup at three call sites. `drive_cut` (:7264) and `drive_owed_cut` (:7296) also repeat the same session/api/keys/vault-signer opening lines. **Fix:** add one helper that returns the pass and the sites together.
6. **Inconsistent constructors, Low** (`facade/owed_rotation.rs`:596). `OwedStop { retryable: true, ..OwedStop::refused(..) }` overrides the meaning of `refused`, while `abandoned` (:67) is its own constructor. **Fix:** add a matching `pending(detail)` constructor.
7. **Possible Mysterious Name, Low** (`facade/owed_rotation.rs`:387). `owed_cut_stands` reads as a yes/no check but returns `Result&lt;(), EngineError&gt;`. **Fix:** rename it to `allow_behind_owed_cut`.
8. **Possible Duplicated Code, Low** (`sync/owed_rotation.rs`, `Standing.check()`, vs `EngineError::rotation_work_owed()`). `from_owed_record(Standing)` and `rotation_work_owed()` build the same error. **Fix:** keep one of them.
9. **Possible Duplicated Code, Low** (`net/renewal_walk.rs`, `owed_scopes`). It builds the `OwedRotation` struct by hand, the same as `ConversionPass::owed()` (`facade/owed_rotation.rs`:149). **Fix:** add a shared constructor.

The `GrantCutPlan::over` fold left no hand-written `GrantCutPlan` literals behind in the touched files. `is_post_publish`, `promote_grantee_scope`, `Landed` and `OwedStep::check` are all fully gone, with no dead references left.</result>
